explanation: Use Euclid’s identity gcd(x,y) = gcd(y,x mod y). When the second value becomes zero, the first is the greatest common divisor.
timeComplexity: O(log(max(x,y))) time for nonzero inputs. Operand bit length decreases through Euclidean remainders or binary-GCD halving; big-integer arithmetic costs are separate.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Iterative variants keep a constant number of integer values; recursive binary variants keep O(B) frames.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: For y>0, x and y have exactly the same common divisors as y and x mod y. Each remainder is smaller than y, so repeated replacement terminates. At y=0, x is the greatest common divisor under the corpus’s zero-input convention.
walkthrough: For (84,30), the remainders are 24, then 6, then 0. The pairs become (30,24), (24,6), (6,0), so return 6.
edgeCases: Either nonnegative operand may be zero; gcd(0,0)=0.
The callable returns BigInt; the judge serializes the integer value.
Use exact JSON integer decoding for values beyond the Number safe-integer range.
